text: Pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff usually indicate the container exits shortly after start. Check logs with kubectl logs --previous to see the last run before the restart.
An OOMKilled status (exit code 137) means the container exceeded its memory limit. Raise resources.limits.memory or fix the leak in the application.
ImagePullBackOff happens when the kubelet cannot fetch the container image. Verify the image tag exists and that imagePullSecrets grant access to the private registry.
Use a HorizontalPodAutoscaler (HPA) to scale replicas based on CPU or custom metrics. The metrics-server must be installed for CPU-based scaling to work.
A PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) limits how many pods a voluntary disruption, such as a node drain, can evict at once, protecting availability during maintenance.
kubectl port-forward svc/myservice 8080:80 tunnels a local port to a service inside the cluster, which is handy for debugging without exposing an Ingress.
Readiness probes gate traffic: a pod failing its readinessProbe is removed from Service endpoints but is not restarted. Liveness probe failures trigger restarts.
Taints and tolerations keep pods off unsuitable nodes. A node tainted with NoSchedule rejects pods that do not declare a matching toleration.
Error 40P01 deadlock_detected means two transactions each hold a lock the other needs. Postgres aborts one; retry it and keep lock acquisition order consistent.
Use EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) to see the actual query plan with timing and I/O. A Seq Scan on a large table in a hot path usually calls for an index.
VACUUM reclaims storage from dead tuples left by updates and deletes. Autovacuum normally handles this; table bloat suggests its thresholds need tuning.
A connection pooler such as PgBouncer in transaction mode lets thousands of clients share a small number of real Postgres connections, avoiding too_many_connections errors.
Set statement_timeout to kill runaway queries before they exhaust resources. It can be set per session, per role, or globally in postgresql.conf.
pg_dump produces a logical backup of one database; pg_basebackup copies the whole cluster for physical replication or point-in-time recovery with WAL archiving.
Index-only scans work when the visibility map shows pages are all-visible and the index covers every selected column. Add INCLUDE columns to widen coverage.
HTTP 429 Too Many Requests means the client is rate limited. Honor the Retry-After header and apply exponential backoff with jitter before retrying.
HTTP 502 Bad Gateway indicates the proxy got an invalid response from the upstream server, often because the backend crashed or closed the connection early.
HTTP 503 Service Unavailable signals temporary overload or maintenance. Unlike 502, the server itself refuses work; a Retry-After header may say when to come back.
A 301 redirect is permanent and cached aggressively by browsers; a 302 is temporary. Use 308 and 307 when the request method must be preserved.
CORS preflight is an OPTIONS request the browser sends before cross-origin calls with custom headers. The server must answer with Access-Control-Allow-Origin and allowed methods.
ETag headers enable conditional requests: the client sends If-None-Match, and the server replies 304 Not Modified when the resource is unchanged, saving bandwidth.
HSTS (Strict-Transport-Security) tells browsers to use HTTPS only for the domain for max-age seconds, preventing protocol downgrade attacks.
git rebase -i lets you squash, reorder, or reword commits before pushing. Never rebase commits that are already shared on a branch others pull from.
git bisect runs a binary search across commit history to find the commit that introduced a bug. Mark commits good or bad and git narrows the range.
A detached HEAD state means you checked out a commit rather than a branch. Create a branch with git switch -c to keep any new commits reachable.
git stash saves uncommitted changes so you can switch branches cleanly. Use git stash pop to reapply, or git stash apply to keep the stash entry.
The error 'non-fast-forward' on push means the remote has commits you lack. Run git pull --rebase to replay your work on top, then push again.
git cherry-pick applies a single commit from another branch onto the current one, useful for backporting a fix to a release branch.
Multi-stage Docker builds keep images small: compile in a builder stage, then COPY --from=builder only the artifacts into a slim runtime image.
The exec form ENTRYPOINT ["app"] runs the process as PID 1 so it receives SIGTERM directly. The shell form wraps it in /bin/sh, which swallows signals.
docker system prune -a removes stopped containers, unused networks, dangling and unreferenced images. Add --volumes to also delete unused volumes.
Bind mounts map a host path into the container and reflect live edits; named volumes are managed by Docker and are the right choice for database data.
A .dockerignore file keeps node_modules, .git, and build output out of the build context, making docker build dramatically faster for large repos.
HEALTHCHECK instructions let the engine mark a container unhealthy; orchestrators can then restart it or stop routing traffic to it.
An S3 presigned URL grants time-limited access to a private object without exposing credentials. The URL embeds a signature and an expiry timestamp.
AWS Lambda cold starts add latency when a new execution environment is created. Provisioned concurrency keeps environments warm for latency-sensitive paths.
IAM policies follow least privilege: grant specific actions on specific resource ARNs. A wildcard Action with Resource '*' is almost always a mistake.
The error AccessDenied from S3 often comes from a bucket policy, not the IAM policy. Both must allow the action, and an explicit Deny anywhere wins.
DynamoDB throttles requests that exceed provisioned capacity with ProvisionedThroughputExceededException. Switch to on-demand mode or add retries with backoff.
Use AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store for credentials instead of environment variables baked into AMIs or task definitions.
A Python virtual environment isolates dependencies per project. Create one with python -m venv .venv and activate it before running pip install.
The GIL (Global Interpreter Lock) prevents CPython threads from running Python bytecode in parallel. Use multiprocessing or asyncio for CPU-bound and I/O-bound work respectively.
Mutable default arguments like def f(items=[]) are evaluated once at definition time and shared across calls. Use None as the default and create the list inside.
ModuleNotFoundError after pip install usually means the package went to a different interpreter. Check with python -m pip install to target the right one.
Use functools.lru_cache to memoize pure functions. For Python 3.9+, functools.cache is an unbounded variant with less overhead.
Context managers via the with statement guarantee cleanup: files close and locks release even when an exception is raised inside the block.
pytest fixtures inject reusable setup into tests. Scope them to function, module, or session to control how often expensive resources are created.
ECONNREFUSED means the target machine actively rejected the TCP connection: nothing is listening on that port, or a firewall sent a reset.
ETIMEDOUT during connect usually means packets are being dropped silently, often by a security group or firewall that lacks an allow rule for the port.
DNS propagation delays come from TTL caching. Lower the record TTL before a migration so resolvers pick up the new address quickly.
TLS handshake failures with ERR_SSL_VERSION_OR_CIPHER_MISMATCH mean client and server share no common protocol version or cipher suite. Enable TLS 1.2 or 1.3 on the server.
MTU mismatches cause large packets to be dropped while small ones pass, producing hangs on big transfers. Path MTU discovery can be broken by ICMP filtering.
A SYN flood exhausts the server's half-open connection queue. SYN cookies let the kernel respond without allocating state until the handshake completes.
Store passwords with a slow adaptive hash such as bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2id. Fast hashes like SHA-256 alone are unsuitable for password storage.
SQL injection is prevented by parameterized queries (prepared statements). Escaping strings by hand is error-prone and should never be the primary defense.
JWT tokens signed with HS256 use a shared secret; RS256 uses an RSA key pair so services can verify tokens without being able to mint them.
CSRF attacks ride the victim's cookies. Defend with SameSite=Lax or Strict cookies and anti-CSRF tokens on state-changing requests.
AES-256-GCM provides authenticated encryption: it detects tampering as well as hiding content. Never reuse a nonce with the same key in GCM mode.
Rotate API keys regularly and scope them narrowly. A leaked key with read-only access to one resource is a far smaller incident than a root credential.
Dense embeddings capture semantic similarity: 'car' and 'automobile' land close together even though they share no characters.
Sparse vectors like BM25 or SPLADE excel at exact term matching, which keeps rare keywords, product codes, and acronyms findable.
Hybrid search fuses dense and sparse results, commonly with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), so you get semantic recall without losing exact-match precision.
HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) graphs power approximate nearest neighbor search with logarithmic-like query time at high recall.
Quantization such as int8 or binary compresses vectors to cut memory use severalfold, trading a small amount of recall for large cost savings.
Payload filtering restricts vector search to points matching metadata conditions, like category = 'billing', without a separate database roundtrip.
The three pillars of observability are logs, metrics, and traces. Correlate them with a shared trace ID to follow one request across services.
P99 latency reveals tail behavior that averages hide: one slow dependency can make the P99 ten times the median while the mean barely moves.
OpenTelemetry (OTel) standardizes instrumentation: one SDK emits traces, metrics, and logs that any compatible backend can ingest.
Alert on symptoms users feel, like error rate and latency SLO burn, rather than causes like CPU usage, to cut noisy pages.
Exit code 137 means the process was killed by SIGKILL (128 + 9), most often by the kernel OOM killer. Check dmesg for 'Out of memory' lines.
File descriptors leak when sockets or files are not closed; ulimit -n shows the cap and ls /proc/PID/fd counts what a process holds open.
systemctl status shows a unit's state and recent log lines; journalctl -u name -f follows the full log stream for that service.
A zombie process has exited but its parent has not called wait(). Zombies hold only a process table slot; reap them by fixing or restarting the parent.
chmod 600 restricts a file to its owner for read and write. SSH refuses private keys with looser permissions, failing with 'UNPROTECTED PRIVATE KEY FILE'.
Cache dependency directories between CI runs keyed on the lockfile hash; a changed lockfile invalidates the cache so builds stay reproducible.
Blue-green deployment keeps two identical environments; traffic flips to the new one atomically and rolls back by flipping the router back.
Canary releases send a small slice of traffic to the new version first, watching error rates and latency before ramping to 100 percent.
Flaky tests erode trust in CI. Quarantine them, track failure rates, and fix root causes like shared state, timing assumptions, and unseeded randomness.
